newsitem.title: JAPAN: DLR SLIGHTLY HIGHER IN TOKYO AS BUBA REPO AWAITED.
newsitem.headline: DLR SLIGHTLY HIGHER IN TOKYO AS BUBA REPO AWAITED.

text.p: 0620 GMT TRADED HIGH/LOW AS OF 0600 GMT
The dollar rose slightly against the mark and the yen by late Tokyo on Tuesday but gains were limited as trading energy ebbed in a thin summer market, dealers said.
The market cautiously awaited the announcement of the Bundesbank's money market operation later in the day for clues to its currency and monetary policy, they added.

Dealers said some traders are holding on to their dollar short positions amid fears that the German central bank may announce at 0700 GMT a variable repo rate. Such a move would fuel speculation that the Bundesbank will raise money rates to prevent the mark from weakening further.

But many dealers in Tokyo believe that the Bundesbank will stick to the current fixed rate of three percent amid weak economic fundamentals in Germany. A bank dealer said ensuring economic recovery is more important for the Bundesbank than guiding rates higher to defend its currency.
If the Bundesbank decides to float money market rates, the rate will be announced on Wednesday.

The dealer said overseas traders, possibly from the Middle East, bought dollars against the mark in late trade after they confirmed that the dollar's downside was solid following a steep fall on Friday. Meanwhile, there was talk of selling interest by German corporations and European central banks, capping the dollar's upside near 1.8680 marks.
The dollar posted modest gains against the yen in late trade on speculative buying amid talk that Japan's economic recovery will be slower than market expectations, dealers said.
But selling interest from U.S. funds limited the greenback's advance against the yen, dealers said. There was talk that a major New York-based hedge fund was placing offers at around 116.30 yen.
In late trade, the Bundesbank said it set the repo tender at an unchanged fixed rate of three percent. The German central bank gave no further immediate comments on money market acitivities.
The dollar jumped towards 1.87 marks immediately after the announcement. By 0705 GMT, the greenback stood near 1.8680/90 marks.
Overseas traders were behind active purchases in reaction to the Buba announcement, a dealer at a Japanese long-term credit bank said.
The dollar closed at 116.10/15 yen and 1.8625/35 marks in New York on Monday.
